original_defect.description: The original reference describes an emitted amplitude at a 'prior bond label a' and then sums over a. It fails to distinguish the free output-bond label from the summed prior input-bond label, while rubric r2 requires the collapsed amplitude formula.

substantive_reconstruction.matrix_orientation: Stage rows are output (new bit c, output bond b), columns are input (fresh bit d, prior bond a), and the passive old prefix is acted on by the identity. The appended bit is the highest emitted wire.
substantive_reconstruction.collapse: Padding E(v)(p,(d,a)) is v(p,a) for d=0 and zero for d=1. Expanding (I tensor U)E(v) at prefix p and output (c,b) makes the passive-prefix sum collapse by its Kronecker delta and the fresh-input-bit sum collapse to d=0. The resulting expression is sum_a U((c,b),(0,a))*v(p,a). For the full word x, p=Fin.init x and c=x(Fin.last n). Thus b is free and a alone is summed.
substantive_reconstruction.norm_argument: The padding mass is sum_{p,d,a} conjugate(E(v)(p,(d,a)))*E(v)(p,(d,a)). The d=1 summands vanish and d=0 reproduces each old (p,a) summand exactly once, giving the old mass for any complex v without a normalization premise. It is a deterministic isometric register embedding, not conditional projection. A subsequent arbitrary U need not preserve mass; full-stage norm preservation requires an appropriate isometry condition on the occupied input subspace, with full unitarity a sufficient condition.
substantive_reconstruction.completion_boundary: Changing input-bit-one columns cannot affect this fresh-zero action. Such columns are unconstrained by this action, but are constrained by separately requested full unitarity. The repair correctly distinguishes those two statements.
substantive_reconstruction.edge_cases: At n=0 the prefix set has one empty word and the same sum applies. Empty bond sets yield zero mass on both sides. Arbitrary complex phases are retained in the linear formula; no global-phase quotient or normalization adjustment is performed.
